subject.title: fix(exec): stop isolated state dirs from moving live approvals

question: Should an explicitly operator-invoked approval migration remain supported when intentionally relocating the primary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, or should every state directory now be permanently independent?
rationale: The PR changes a shipped, documented migration contract and the resulting approval policy for relocated installations, so code review alone cannot choose the permanent trust and upgrade boundary.

options.title: Preserve explicit relocation
options.body: Keep automatic and implicit paths fully isolated, but retain a narrowly user-confirmed doctor import for intentional primary-state moves.

options.title: Adopt permanent isolation
options.body: Remove all cross-state imports, explicitly accept the compatibility break, and provide a safe visible upgrade/import workflow for affected users.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit relocation
recommendation.body: Keep automatic and implicit paths fully isolated, but retain a narrowly user-confirmed doctor import for intentional primary-state moves.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored both the prior merged boundary design and the current broader isolation proposal.
